correctness.rationale: For all n>=5, KG(n,2) has distance one for disjoint pairs and distance two for intersecting pairs. Reconstructing the selected-geodesic condition rules out all two-set selections; any selected triple with two intersecting ground edges has an outside witness lacking an admissible 2-geodesic. Three pairwise disjoint edges work precisely when only zero or one ground vertex is unused, i.e. n=6,7, with counts 15 and 105. The universal four-set {12,13,23,45} works for every n>=5 by the cases on an outside pair's ground support. The reported lower and upper bounds and extremizer classification follow for arbitrary n, not from finite checking. Independent direct graph-geodesic enumeration for n=5,6,7,8 found respectively 0,15,105,0 dominating triples and checked the four-set at n=5,8. Reviewed exact RESULT.md and verify.py from the pinned Git commit; no all-four-minimizer claim.
